approach: Add a family check to Config::validate (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs:639), after the hard_producer_model check at :670-674. Config::parse runs validate on every load (:616-619). The check matches lowercase substrings opus, sonnet and haiku across reader, producer_default, producer_allowed, verifier and hard_producer_model. A missing family returns a new ConfigError::ModelFamily(&'static str). Config unit tests edit REPO_CONFIG text to drop each family. A new integration test, crates/athena-core/tests/model_roster.rs, loads the repository athena.toml through the real loader, checks a haiku-less copy is refused, checks the OLY-B-SET-02 spec entry (parsed from its measure value with the closing quote trimmed), and checks jev::ENDPOINT and jev::MODEL. jev.rs, lib.rs, athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows and briefs.rs stay unchanged. docs/spec.toml gets a real mechanism and a measure ending `status: not shown`. xtask/shard-timings.txt gets the new unit. CHANGELOG.md gets an entry. This revision lists all non-test readers of Config::parse in the dependents (gate content rule, trailers_stopped, cutover_job_for and its callers, xtask setup) and names the tests and the CI history job that cover them.

decisions.choice: Enforce the roles in Config::validate with ConfigError::ModelFamily(&'static str), matching lowercase substrings on reader, producer_default, producer_allowed, verifier and hard_producer_model. The message states that the rule applies to every athena.toml Athena loads and says how to satisfy it. The CHANGELOG entry says the same.
decisions.reason: validate is the one non-test reader every load reaches: Config::parse (config.rs:616), config_at (athena-gate/src/lib.rs:184), JobConfig::at (capability.rs:41), admission (admission.rs:933), the gate content rule (content.rs:99, :133), trailers_stopped (invariant.rs:832), cutover_job_for (gh/records.rs:314), xtask setup (xtask/src/main.rs:184) and the user-repository load (athena-cli/src/wiring.rs:206). The rule is global on purpose: the requirement is Athena's own model set. A version bump such as claude-opus-5-6 keeps passing because no id list is used. [models] has no serde default for reader, producer_default, producer_allowed or verifier (config.rs:314-318), so every parsing config has the fields the check reads.

rejected.option: A hard-coded ROSTER constant in jev.rs checked by a test (prior job 20261030-001211-6mzd)
rejected.why: Nothing read it, so removing a model from the real config left the test green.

rejected.option: Match exact ids such as claude-opus-5-5
rejected.why: Every model upgrade would need a code change; the spec names families, not versions.

rejected.option: Count the keys of [models.names] as roles
rejected.why: That table is display text for trailers (athena.toml:28-32). A stale entry there would hide a missing role.

rejected.option: Apply the rule only to this repository, for example in an xtask or a test
rejected.why: Nothing at load time would refuse a config that dropped a family: the no-reader shape again.

decisions.choice: Cover the readers that load past or parent configs with named existing tests plus the CI job `athena check --history` (ci.yml:606-607). Add no athena-gate test. State that trailers_stopped (invariant.rs:829-833) and cutover_job_for (gh/records.rs:312-318) fall back silently on a refused config (`.ok()` gives false or None), and accept that with a reason: both read only whether `[history] cutover_job` is set, and that key exists only in current-era configs, which descend from the present athena.toml with all three families. A parent config that lacked a family would already return false/None before the cutover key existed. The history evidence rests on docs/decisions.md:325-327 and :725-726 (Haiku and Sonnet producers, Opus verifier from v0) and on the CI history job. The old validate rules (verifier outside producer_allowed, default inside it) are not used as evidence, since they say nothing about families.
decisions.reason: check_history_with_exempt (history.rs:235-243) judges every commit, and the content rule (content.rs:93-102) calls Config::parse on every commit that touches athena.toml, raising Rule::Configuration for a refusal. A past commit whose athena.toml named no opus, sonnet or haiku model would be reported by `athena check --history`. HISTORY.txt shows paths, not contents, so old text cannot be read here. If the CI history job fails on an old commit, the producer reports it and does not weaken the rule.

rejected.option: Add an athena-gate test with a parent athena.toml lacking a family
rejected.why: It edits athena-gate, which is not a deliverable. Gate fixtures already build on BUILTIN_CONFIG (the real athena.toml), so they keep all three families.

rejected.option: Make trailers_stopped and cutover_job_for report a refusal instead of falling back
rejected.why: Out of scope and a behavior change in the gate and landing; the fallback is safe for configs that carry the families.

decisions.choice: Keep Jev shadow-only. The Jev clause is shown by asserting the existing jev::ENDPOINT and jev::MODEL in model_roster.rs. No HTTP-client words appear in new comments or test text.
decisions.reason: Making Jev decide work is out of scope. external_calls_guard.rs:13-16 scans every .rs file under crates/ for reqwest, ureq, hyper, isahc, attohttpc, surf, curl, minreq, http_req and Command::new("gh").

rejected.option: Add Jev to [models] or to the family check
rejected.why: It would change athena.toml and put Jev on real work.

decisions.choice: Add `athena-core --test model_roster 5.00` to xtask/shard-timings.txt between external_calls_guard and refusal_corpus.
decisions.reason: xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:410-421 asserts the timed units equal the workspace targets exactly. The value is an estimate.

rejected.option: Put the athena-core check inside the lib tests
rejected.why: Criterion 4 names `cargo test -p athena-core --test model_roster`, which needs an integration test file.

decisions.choice: The spec check in model_roster.rs slices docs/spec.toml from `id = "OLY-B-SET-02"` to the next `[[requirement]]`, takes the line starting `measure = `, strips the prefix and trims the trailing quote (and whitespace), then asserts the value ends with `status: not shown`. It also asserts the slice lacks `mechanism = "none"` and contains `Config::validate`.
decisions.reason: Entries are written as `measure = "...; status: requirement"` (spec.toml:2023), so the raw line ends in a quote and a plain ends_with fails on a correct entry (finding 2). xtask/tests/spec.rs:204-210 and :627-655 accept the literal none, so passing them does not show the entry changed.

rejected.option: Parse the block with toml_edit or the hestia parse_spec
rejected.why: More machinery for one line; trimming the quote is enough, and the test panics with a readable message when the id is missing.

rejected.option: Rely on cargo test -p xtask --test spec alone
rejected.why: It passes whether or not the entry changed.

risks.risk: A past athena.toml may lack a family by name, so `athena check --history` would report a Configuration violation for that commit (content.rs:99, history.rs:239-242). HISTORY.txt lists paths, not contents, so old text was not checked.
risks.mitigation: docs/decisions.md:325-327 and :725-726 record Haiku and Sonnet producers and an Opus verifier from v0. The match is a substring, so version bumps pass. CI `athena check --history` (ci.yml:606-607) and `cargo test -p athena-gate` are the named checks. If the history job fails on an old commit, the producer reports it and does not weaken the rule silently.

risks.risk: trailers_stopped (invariant.rs:829-833) and cutover_job_for (gh/records.rs:313-317) turn a refused parent config into false or None without a report. That would change whether Athena- trailers are required and whether the cutover runs.
risks.mitigation: Both read only `[history] cutover_job`, which exists only in current-era configs that carry all three families. Gate and landing tests (invariant.rs:1016-1031, gh/tests.rs:4107-4179, cutover_fixture.rs:216-222) build on the real athena.toml and pass through the check. The CI history job would show any commit where it changes.

risks.risk: A future model alias without opus, sonnet or haiku in its name would be refused.
risks.mitigation: The error names the family and says how to satisfy the rule. The match is a case-insensitive substring, so version bumps and vendor prefixes pass. An alias change needs a deliberate edit of the rule.

risks.risk: A text-replacement test passes for the wrong reason if the pattern misses or another error fires first.
risks.mitigation: The helper asserts the text changed. Each case asserts the exact ModelFamily variant and family. The opus case uses a verifier outside producer_allowed, so VerifierCanProduce cannot fire first.

risks.risk: Comments or test text that describe the Jev constants use an HTTP-client word and fail external_calls_guard.
risks.mitigation: Steps 2 and 4 forbid those words; external_calls_guard is in the producer's check list.

risks.risk: The spec check depends on the layout of docs/spec.toml (the id line, the next `[[requirement]]` header, a single-line `measure = "..."`).
risks.mitigation: It slices on those markers, the layout of the entries at :2019-2026, trims the closing quote, and panics with a readable message if the id or the measure line is not found.

risks.risk: The 5.00 s timing for the new shard unit is a guess.
risks.mitigation: The file header already marks the values as estimates; the CHANGELOG labels the value as an estimate.

demonstrations.seam: Entry points: athena_data::Config::parse and the pub consts athena_core::jev::ENDPOINT and MODEL (jev.rs:31-33). athena-data is a normal dependency of athena-core, so an integration test can use it. No fake. The consts and loader exist; the test file is added by plan step 4.

demonstrations.method: Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Also run `cargo test -p xtask --test spec`, `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`, `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test external_calls_guard`, `cargo test -p athena-gate`, `cargo test -p athena-core` (gh/tests.rs cutover tests, admission tests), `cargo test -p athena-cli` (cutover_fixture, trailer_stop) and `cargo test -p athena-data --test repo_config`. The CI job `athena check --history` is the check that covers past configs; it runs in CI and cannot be run here. The rule is a config check on structured TOML, not a request parser, so no refusal_corpus case applies; `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is run only as a regression check and I read no corpus case for it.
demonstrations.observes: No formatting diff, no clippy warnings, a full green run. ci_shards' checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit sees the model_roster line. external_calls_guard passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the shard-timings line, checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit fails. An HTTP-client word in the new files fails external_calls_guard.
